body.p: Three big Walla. Once upon a time there lived three brothers Wella. The elder Wella had a wife â a woman from the Calf's Eye clan. The middle one also had a wife â a woman from the de Bullseye tribe, and the youngest did not yet have his own tent. Once the elder Walla said to his wife: âLook at your head!â And the wife says: âWhat am I going to watch there? If you have something to say, just say it." Then the elder Walla spoke thus: "I want to go to the lands from which you come, to the lands of the calf's eye, to take a wife for my younger brother, to marry him off." The Calf's Eye Woman says, âWhat are you talking about? Those who left for the lands of Calf's Eyes remained there forever. They don't come back from there. My father, at the time of his youth and strength, brought me here.â But the elder Walla is unlikely to ever listen to a woman's advice. In the morning it was still dark, the elder Valla cleared his empty sledges from the snow. He says: âOur matchmakers Calf's Eye won't touch us. I'm still going to get married." He went there. The bullet flew there. He came to the lands of the Calf's Eyes. No one climbs to him, people seemed peaceful, he wooed. The youger brother was engaged to a woman. They didn't stay there long. They went back. And the Calf's Eye family went to war behind them. They began to fight, almost all Wella were killed. Only the wife of the middle brother with a child was able to escape. So the Calf's Eyes began to pursue her. There were fir trees at the bottom of the ravine. They spent the night there. Her deer turned out to be long-haired. These two bulls themselves ate reindeer moss in the camping spot lots. Suddenly she saw in the distance two chasing warriors. She harnessed two Longhairs and ran along the bottom of the ravine. A woman resembling a man along the bottom of the ravine rushed like an arrow. As they were running along the bottom of the ravine, somewhere around the bend, the baby fell out. After some time, the woman discovered that the child was not in the sled. She turned her long-haired ones and went on her way. The woman Bull's Sight went back to look for her child. She found it and saw: the child's arms were broken, his legs were broken, so they left him there. You look there, only his eyes blink. Why did they torture her baby, only its eyes blink. And the enemies turned him back. She put the child on the sled and ran away with it. It is not known how long she traveled, she was so hungry, she wished for death. Her clothes were sewn from the skin, from the otter, she scorched her with a flint and so satisfied her hunger. She thought: âItâs like Iâve been going for thirty years.â The baby's breathing has become uneven, but the heart is still working. She didn't want to leave him. She drove on and saw a big lake. This lake was called the Lake of Spirits. Thirty sledges stand on the shore of this huge lake, a load is tied to them: larch logs, everything is tied with horseskins, covered with birchbark. Although everything was tied, she still tied. Bullish Glance built a huge house. She put her child there. She looks at him: still alive. How many years they lived like this is unknown, they fed him with meager food. She watched him: he became a big man, albeit a sick one. Once she remained in the tent, and someone quietly comes in from under the fabric door and looks around. Her hem is one span, her back is also one span. Looking at it, she realized that this is a woman, here is the Bullish Glance, and she thought: âThe hem is one span, the back is one span, who are you?â She entered the tent, she turned out to be a woman. She tells them: âTomorrow the Calf's Eye will come to you with war. I will come to help you." So she said, darted under the door flap, as if no one was there. The next day he looks: beyond that huge lake of ice is not visible, everything has become like summer, the soldiers, holding their bows, are moving forward. Bull's Sight thought, "One child can do what." She started to wake up, woke up. She woke up, her arms began to stretch, her joints clicked. To his mother, he said: "Give me a bow!" âBut they have a lot of bows.â Still, his mother gave him a bow. Her mother looks at her: one of her eyes is crookedly overgrown. So the mother says: âYou donât have a name. Let your name be Crooked Walla. She herself thought: âOne child will do what. But I just look: this crooked Vella is brave and dexterous. One arrow, which is directed at him, leans back, the other passes by, bending around him. Like a fish twisting on ice, the warriors cannot catch it at all. Crooked Valla shoots with a bow so that he kills five warriors with one arrowhead, they fall on the ice. The ice of that lake, the Lake of Spirits, was trampled all over, covered with blood. The leaders of those warriors are all covered in blood, the two brothers of Calf's Eyes ran away, only they were seen. That's where he killed everyone. This Crooked Walla turned out to be the Spirit of Heaven. If he looks with a crooked eye, there is thunder and lightning in the sky, if he looks with a good look â a sunny day. The woman, whose hem is one span and her back is one span, turned out to be the Grandmother of the Earth, she helped the two of them. The woman of the Bull's eyes is the heavenly woman Kazym, the woman of the Kazym Spirit. And this lake is called Sacred Lake. On the hill that is near this lake, the Spirit of the sky â Num sits. On the hill of the sacred lake now resides.
